card.name: Start of 'acute' in overdose text
card.fires_on: The first piece of the word 'acute' (Ac, ac) when it is split into pieces, mostly in overdose or toxicity sections. Also fires weakly on other word starts like 'alk' and 'Abs'.

modes.label: Acute split at start of sentence
modes.description: Capitalized 'Ac' beginning 'Acute' right after a sentence about overdose or toxicity.
modes.example: The oral LD 50 of hydrochlorothiazide is greater than 10 g/kg in both mice and rats.<< Ac>>ute overdosage of spironol

modes.label: Acute inside a sentence
modes.description: Lowercase 'ac' beginning 'acutely' within a toxicity statement.
modes.example: One death was reported in a man who may have taken as much as 10 g<< ac>>utely.

modes.label: Other a- word starts
modes.description: Other words beginning with a, such as alkalosis or absorption, in the same overdose setting.
modes.example: Dosage and rate of administration should be carefully supervised to avoid overtreatment (<<alk>>alosis).

card.plain: It marks the start of the word 'acute' when an overdose or toxicity passage is being read.
